gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-noto-tradi: Loud, gapped, unmistakable. Electroharmonix breaks each word into separate letters for maximum punch, while Noto Traditional Nushu keeps a broad-nibbed sans-serif stroke whose bowls fill the line and never curl shut.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-numans: Striking letters, split apart one by one. Numans follows in a plain sans with tracking pushed far past normal, and that stretched-out spacing is the quality that most sets the pair up.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-onest: Onest keeps its ascenders short above big bowls, drawn with a gentle monotone line. Electroharmonix is the one for commanding, gap-split display letters, while Onest does its best work as the quiet sans underneath.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-orienta: Commanding from the first glance, Electroharmonix splits every word into single letters. Orienta takes over with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open, and with little height difference between its cases, it is the plain sans doing the steady work.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-oxygen: Gapped, loud and open-handed in every curve. Oxygen then arrives with curves that never close back on themselves, and its lowercase nearly matches the capitals, which is what makes the pair feel so uncluttered.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-parkinsans: Electroharmonix breaks each word into single letters with open-handed curves, while the sans-serif below is drawn as if with one marker tip. Parkinsans feels crisp and tidy beside it, a tidy counterweight to the loud heading.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-pathway-ex: Pathway Extreme has clear openings in its rounded letters and stubby ascenders next to a big x-height. Pathway Extreme sits beneath the gap-split, commanding Electroharmonix like a compact sans anchoring a page that wants to shout.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-preahvihea: Preahvihear opens its letter mouths like a pried oyster shell and lifts its x-height high. Over a long page it stays inviting, and Electroharmonix handles the striking, gapped opening above it.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-prompt: Prompt gives its small letters an oversized look, with open apertures that are easily readable. Prompt and Electroharmonix share a generous openness, and that shared quality, loud in one and quiet in the other, is the pair's strongest.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-pt-sans-ca: PT Sans Caption reads with unclosed, inviting bowls and big-bodied lowercase letters. Electroharmonix does its best work splitting words into striking, commanding single letters, while PT Sans Caption does its best work carrying the text underneath.
